analysis:
Examined the test edits, the new release-lane scripts and the publication changes. No concrete regression found; the key conclusions rest on code outside this batch.

scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh runs the signed app's CLI under `env -i` with a throwaway HOME. It makes the output folder with plain `mkdir`, so an existing folder fails, and `set -euo pipefail` is on. It adds no network or secret exposure.

scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-models.py (lines 60-173) reads the environment's coordinator and CDN URLs from provider-identity.json. Redirects are refused, responses are size-capped, and candidates must name the catalog entry id and the listed aggregate. config.json must match the manifest's size and SHA-256. A catalog entry with no usable manifest fails the whole run. A listed model missing from the catalog is dropped and named in skipped.md, which fails toward fewer pair-serving grants. The script never recomputes the aggregate hash from the manifest file list. It also does not require https. Whether the app's worker re-verifies the aggregate and chooses among candidates (ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts) is outside the supplied evidence. That matters because T-054 and A-017 qualifications and the T-053 pair-serving grant are derived from this CDN and coordinator-supplied metadata. `r2_prefix` is percent-quoted per segment but a `..` segment is not rejected. That only affects which CDN object is fetched, and the manifest and hash checks still gate it.

scripts/provider-release-publication.py (lines 24-185, 215-228) adds strict validation of the cluster_runtime block: exact field sets, digests that are lowercase hex and non-zero, sorted and unique model IDs, byte-canonical JSON with duplicate-key rejection, a 64 KiB bound, a derived-ID length bound, and a registration-body size check before staging. The block is read before any folder is written. `--cluster-runtime` is limited to `prepare`. The script computes no digests and depends on the coordinator's own validation and the RELEASE_KEY boundary (A-005, A-011), which is outside this batch. `registration_body` keeps the old encoding when the block is absent.

The Swift test changes only add fixtures and test cases for assistant planning. They have no security impact.

Open question: whether the producing app CLI and the coordinator enforce the same qualification semantics (T-052, T-054, T-057).
